title: Find your way around RSE
introduction: Explore the browser, libraries, workspace, properties and project toolbar. Start in any open project; this tour does not create model elements.

steps.title: The model browser
steps.content: The browser shows the model hierarchy. Packages organise elements; expand a package with its arrow to see its contents. This is your main route to selecting model elements.

steps.title: Explore the libraries
steps.content: Use this icon to switch the left panel to libraries. Libraries contain reusable modelling elements and definitions. Click the icon in RSE, or use Open libraries below.

steps.title: Return to your model
steps.content: Switch back to the model browser to continue working with your own elements. The sidebar icons switch between different tools in the same area.

steps.title: Filter the browser
steps.content: The funnel opens browser filters. Filters change what you see in the browser; they do not delete elements. Try opening it, then close it when you are ready to continue.

steps.title: The workspace and views
steps.content: The central workspace contains tabs for model views. Home lists available views. A view presents selected model elements; the elements belong to the model and can appear in several views.

steps.title: Inspect and edit properties
steps.content: Selecting an element updates this panel. Essential shows its main properties. Additional tabs depend on the selected element. Changes in this panel may need Apply before you save the project.

steps.title: Find model elements
steps.content: Search helps locate an element by name when a project is too large to browse manually. You can then use the result to navigate to that element.

steps.title: Check your model
steps.content: The validation menu provides model checks. These help identify modelling issues; validation is a separate operation from saving.

steps.title: Configurations and changes
steps.content: This menu exposes configuration and change-management operations. Your active configuration is shown nearby. In a practice project, follow your team’s process before committing or discarding changes.

steps.title: Save your work
steps.content: Save records the changes made in your current configuration. It does not by itself commit them to the main configuration. You are ready to try the first-model exercise from the training catalogue.
